links.outcome: Side-by-side comparison of 3 ambient scribe vendors on identical recordings, Likert ratings and error audit
links.effect: Vendor A had highest Likert ratings (Friedman χ²(2)=15.529, P<.001 short visit); audit found fewest errors in Vendor B (n=3), then A (n=8), C (n=9). Vendor rankings differed by method.
links.quote: In this exploratory sample, Vendor A received the highest mean Likert ratings across all 4 domains (Friedman χ²(2) = 15.529, P < .001 short visit; χ²(2) = 10.753, P = .005 long visit).

links.outcome: Audit-identified hallucinations, omissions, and inaccuracies in ambient scribe notes
links.effect: Audit identified errors in all three vendors' notes: Vendor B n=3, Vendor A n=8, Vendor C n=9. Clinician preference did not track audit error counts.
links.quote: The audit identified fewest errors in Vendor B's notes (n = 3), followed by Vendor A (n = 8) and Vendor C (n = 9).

links.outcome: Whether clinician Likert ratings of scribe quality align with transcript-level error audit
links.effect: Clinician ratings did not track audit error counts; physicians flagged hallucinations more often than the audit confirmed ('pseudo-hallucinations'). After Bonferroni correction only Vendor A vs B on short visit remained significant (P=.0098).
links.quote: In this sample, clinician preference did not track audit-identified error counts, raising the hypothesis that note-style features influence ratings alongside documentation correctness; larger samples are required.

unlisted_practices: Pairing clinician Likert ratings with transcript-level manual error audit to evaluate generative AI scribes

screen.reason: The study empirically tests an in-house evaluation and auditing framework (comparing clinician ratings vs manual transcript-level error audits) across commercial ambient digital scribe systems using simulated clinical encounters.

primary.practice: transcript-level error audits paired with clinician evaluation
